task_description: Dogfood the crates.io trusted-publishing path in production: publish checkpoint-template 0.1.0, then verify README, metadata, packaging, docs.rs, and registry consumption against the live service
defects_found_and_fixed: No crate shipped a LICENSE file though every Cargo.toml listed one in include; packages silently dropped their license
Workspace metadata carried Your Name / your-org/your-repo / docs.rs placeholder values that would be permanent on crates.io; template_init rewrites them, so real baseline values preserve portability

The release contract test demanded exit 0 from release-publish without a token, which only passed because the allowlist was empty; it now asserts the invocation parses while keeping zero-exit for config-only commands
mcp-server-template is already owned by another publisher on crates.io and is left publish=false
verification: crates.io API: max_version 0.1.0, license MIT, repository correct, publisher d-oit
README renders on crates.io and packaged .crate contains LICENSE
External consumer crate resolved checkpoint-template 0.1.0 from the registry; README quick-start compiled and round-tripped state
release-publish is idempotent: skips the live version and exits 0
contract test non-vacuity proven by reverting the workflow to the broken --root ordering (exit 2)
notes: Publishing from a dirty tree is correctly refused by cargo; the change was committed before upload so the artifact corresponds to a commit. The crates.io web frontend returns 404 for every crate in this sandbox (serde included), so page-level verification used the API, docs.rs, and the downloaded .crate instead. The `release` environment still requires a repository administrator to create, so the OIDC publish job remains gated on that manual step.
